long_biography.plain_text:
Workshop experience shaped Benson Ford's leadership of Ford Motor Company's Lincoln-Mercury division. During school holidays he worked at River Rouge, then left Princeton for an experimental garage in Dearborn, where he dismantled test engines and helped build a military vehicle. After wartime Army Air Forces service, he returned to the company and took charge of the division.

Ford's public work was centred on Detroit institutions. As president of Henry Ford Hospital's board, he helped secure major funding for medical research and oversaw three decades of growth. He also chaired national community campaigns and served as a national co-chairman of the National Conference of Christians and Jews, making civic service a substantial part of his public life.

uncertainties: Identity is resolved at 100 as Benson Ford Sr. Burger Boat's period publication states that Onika was built for Benson Ford, and the construction record ties the 1966 Onika to the later Aurore name and 91-GT specification in the authoritative record. Contemporary obituary, family, corporate and Michigan sources converge on the American Ford executive born in 1919 and deceased in 1978.

The principal namesake is Benson Ford Jr. Later reporting identifies the son as a separate person who first joined Ford Motor Company in 1986. The elder Ford's 1966 Onika ownership, established executive career, birth and death dates exclude transfer of the son's facts into this record.

The authoritative owner record leaves Aurore's relationship open from 1966 despite Benson Ford Sr.'s death in 1978. The relationship is therefore stale as a current-ownership claim. It is used only as historical identity evidence and is excluded from both biographies, wealth reasoning and public field proposals.

The source record's calculated birth age of 59 paired with a 2020 calculation date is internally stale. It happens to equal Ford's age at death but is not used as evidence; direct birth and death records support the proposed dates and Deceased correction.

Benson Ford is retained as the display name. Later sources often add Sr. to distinguish his son, but contemporaneous records use Benson Ford and do not establish Sr. as a legal or consistently used name suffix. No middle name or suffix is proposed.

Automotive is both the creation and terminal primary industry. Henry Ford's will directly transferred controlling voting stock to Benson and other family members, later reporting places Class B Ford stock at the core of Benson's estate, and his operating career remained with Ford Motor Company. No unsupported estate valuation or precise share count is inferred.

Inherited is directly supported by Henry Ford's voting-stock bequest. The dossier does not claim that this one bequest describes every asset Benson later held, but it establishes inheritance of the principal wealth-producing family asset at very high confidence.

Operator is used instead of Heir / family shareholder because Benson combined inherited ownership with sustained executive responsibility for the core asset as corporate vice-president, director, Lincoln-Mercury leader and dealer-policy chairman. He did not found Ford Motor Company, and his active role is more defining than passive family shareholding.

The primary-industry field describes Ford's principal identifiable private wealth at death because the subject is deceased. It is not presented as a current 2026 holding. Ford Class B stock and the automotive company remained central to his estate and public economic identity at that terminal point.
Main Residence Country is proposed as United States from the contemporary Grosse Pointe Shores home record. No secondary residence is proposed, and yacht location is not used to infer residence.

The exact 27 July 1978 death date follows directly from the Washington Post obituary published on Friday 28 July stating that he died Thursday, independently corroborated by the Grosse Pointe historical record. No death-place field exists in the owner input, so Cheboygan is not proposed.

Forbes-first searches found no dedicated Benson Ford Sr. profile. A Forbes caption names him among Henry Ford's grandsons but is incidental coverage rather than a profile, so no Forbes social row is proposed.

The exact Wikipedia profile is proposed after cross-verification against the yacht, family, date and company evidence. A person who died in 1978 cannot have authentic LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter/X, YouTube, TikTok or personal-site profiles, and no such links are proposed.

Ford is the single minimum useful active tag. It passes the principal-family-owner and defining-long-term-leader contract through inherited voting ownership and sustained operating leadership. Military officer is excluded because wartime service was not his defining public occupation, and no generic philanthropy, family-business or automotive-industry tag is added.
The biographies remain sale-independent and omit Aurore, Onika, yacht specifications, private health details, estate estimates, changing stock values and posthumous family disputes.
